observed_mapping.observation: MatchedInformationSeekingResult stores score_delta, probe_delta and public_payload_novelty_delta as separate evaluator-side measurements.
score_delta is mechanically required to equal intervention.cumulative_score minus baseline.cumulative_score; novelty and probe count do not enter that equality.

WP800 step_episode adds next_node.evaluator_score to cumulative_score on every transition. Therefore probe acquisition cost can already be represented evaluator-side by assigning a negative score to a probe-result/intermediate node without exposing that cost or hidden state to the policy.

The merged positive-path test has baseline score -5, intervention score 10, score_delta +15, probe_delta +1 and novelty_delta +1. It proves useful probing can be discriminated but does not test that novelty/probe count are insufficient when utility does not improve.

PROBE_THEN_COMMIT is a deterministic benchmark policy with public decision rules and a probe budget, not an online Bayesian value-of-information optimizer. This is compatible with WP802 being evaluation infrastructure rather than a runtime cognition policy.

e1_hypothesis_reconciliation.original_hypothesis: WP802 may need primary decision utility net of probe cost instead of novelty/information amount.
details: Decision utility is already represented independently by score_delta.
Probe cost can already be represented inside cumulative evaluator score via intermediate-node evaluator_score.
Novelty/probe count are separate diagnostics and are not algebraically mixed into score_delta.
No heavyweight VoI/POMDP dependency is justified.

proposal: Add a held-out negative-control fixture where probing yields a new public observation (novelty_delta > 0) but its explicit evaluator-side acquisition cost makes score_delta <= 0.
Assert that positive novelty_delta and positive probe_delta do not imply positive score_delta or benchmark superiority.
Add a boundary comment/receipt stating that cumulative score is the decision-utility channel and may include declared probe cost, while novelty/probe counts are diagnostics only.
Do not add a second net_decision_value field unless a future consumer demonstrates ambiguity that cannot be resolved from score_delta semantics; avoid duplicate metrics/authority surfaces.

minimal_fixture_design.probe_path: probe reaches a novel intermediate public observation with evaluator score -15, then informed commit reaches +10
minimal_fixture_design.expected: intervention cumulative score -5, score_delta 0, probe_delta +1, novelty_delta +1
minimal_fixture_design.stronger_variant: use intermediate probe cost -20 so intervention cumulative score -10 and score_delta -5 while novelty_delta remains +1

best_supported_delta.expected_cost: test-only or documentation-only delta; no external dependency, model call, runtime service, extra context payload or resident model

counterhypothesis.statement: The existing separate result fields and positive-path test are sufficient because downstream consumers are already expected to interpret score_delta, probe_delta and novelty_delta independently.
counterhypothesis.cheapest_discriminator: Run the negative-control fixture. If current code naturally emits novelty_delta > 0 with score_delta <= 0 and no consumer/test equates novelty with success, retain source unchanged and add only the regression test/receipt.

next_exact_gate: Atomically claim an E3 claim-reproduction objective for the negative-control invariant, execute the smallest deterministic reproduction against the exact merged WP802/WP800 semantics, and promote only if the result distinguishes novelty/probe activity from net evaluator utility.
